title.narrative: Output 2.4. Increased capacity Member States to apply sectoral international labour standards, codes of practice and guidelines

description.narrative: 1. In line with the WHO-ILO global framework for national occupational health programmes for health workers, 2010, the Government of Pakistan, in consultation with hospital managers and health workers, has successfully implemented a new sectoral initiative - the ILO-WHO HealthWISE tool across three healthcare facilities. These hospitals have not only developed comprehensive medium to long-term action plans but have also taken immediate steps to reform their institutional policies, effectively translating their newfound knowledge and capacity-building into tangible improvements in healthcare delivery. Furthermore, the Government, through the Directorate of Workers Education, has proactively nurtured a cadre of expert professionals trained in HealthWISE, contributing to the sustained enhancement of healthcare practices and outcomes in the region. All three health facilities have established a committee/ working group composed of management and workers representatives to lead and ensure sustainable implementation of the HealthWISE approach. 2. Guidelines for Sanitation workers on OSH practices and FPRW were developed and implemented based on ILO sectoral standards. The ILO has conducted a Comparative assessment study on ILO Nursing Personnel Convention (No. 149). The technical support provided in relation to C149 supported the consideration of the ratification process of C149 and to strengthen the provision of a decent work environment for nursing personnel in Pakistan in line with Pakistan’s goal of achieving Universal Health Coverage. The Nursing Personnel Convention, 1977 (No. 149) is considered on the workplan of the Pakistani Government and targeted for ratification in 2025. Further, a study assessing gender equality in health leadership in Pakistan at institutional, structural, policy, and service delivery levels was conducted and recommendations to address Gender Equality and Leadership Gaps in the health sector in Pakistan at all levels developed. Support from OECD, WHO and ILO on promoting decent work in health sector has mobilised existing ILO -WHO sectoral tools and guidelines for improving working environment and conditions Govt of Japan assisted in developing guidelines on OSH for sanitation workers, this has been possible after series of engagements with employers and workers organizations in the country.

description.narrative: In 2022, a new mechanism was created – the ILS committee of the Government, which includes representatives from federal and provincial government, to work on ILS-related issues, including the reports to the CEACR and addressing CEACR recommendations. The ILS committee is key to ensures tripartite consultations at Provincial Tripartite Consultative Committees and Federal Tripartite Consultative Committee on these issues. In 2023, tripartite constituents discussed Technical Notes (TN) providing recommendations on the implementation of the recommendations of the CEACR on 14 ratified ILO Conventions. In August 2023, series of consultations on freedom of association and collective bargaining (FoACB) discussed the implementation of recommendations of the CEACR on C87 and C98 using the Technical Note on FoACB. . Tripartite committees were established in Sindh and Punjab in 2023 to work on the provincial Labour Law Consolidation; the committees in both provinces have met two times in 2023. Tripartite constituents discussed the gap analyses and ratification of the following Conventions were conducted: C149, C176, C155 and C187, C190. The ILO, with support from the European Union the following technical assistance was provided: • ILO developed terms of reference of the ILS Government Committee. • ILO developed a technical note on the implementation of the latest recommendations of the CEACR concerning 14 ILO Conventions ratified by Pakistan and supported tripartite consultations to discuss needed legislative amendments. • ILO developed the capacity of tripartite constituents at the federal and provincial levels on the ILS supervisory system and reporting obligations through workshops organized in May and June 2022. • ILO conducted a analysis of the gaps and problem areas on FOA/CB and developed a Technical note (TN) on C.87 and C98 for four provinces and federal government and facilitated consultations for government, employers, and workers on the TN in August 2023. • ILO, while providing support to Sindh and Punjab provincial government on consolidation of labour laws, supported establishment of Labour Law reform tripartite committees and tripartite consultations on the planned reform in 2023. • ILO supported establishment of the Trade Unions’ ILS Coordinating Committee through events in September 2022 and August 2023 and capacity building of workers’ and employers’ representatives to participate in ratification and implementation of ILS. • ILO supported tripartite consultations on C149, C176, C155 and C187, C190.

description.narrative: Pakistan UNSDCF 2023-2027 and Pakistan DWCP 2023-22027 include references to the implementation of recommendations of the issues raised by the ILO supervisory bodies, including specific plans and actions. In the UNSDCF 2023-2027, Outcome 4 “Sustainable and inclusive economic growth and decent work”, main intervention strategies for Output 4.6 (“Fundamental principles and rights at work (FPRW) are applied to prevent all forms of exploitation of workers and others in the world of work…”) include “Supporting the implementation of International Labour Standards and national laws on child labour, forced labour, non-discrimination, freedom of association and collective bargaining, minimum wages, occupational safety and health for workers and others engaged in all economic sectors, in line with the recommendations of the ILO’s supervisory bodies. Performance indicator 4.6.3. include “Number of cases for which ILO supervisory bodies or other international bodies notice progress in the implementation of fundamental principles and rights at work” DWCP 2023-2027 has extensive references to addressing issues raised by the ILO supervisory bodies. • DWCP’s Priority 3 “Strengthening the application of international labour standards (ILS), fundamental principles and rights at work (FPRW), and harmonious industrial relations” has related three outputs (3.1.1, 3.1.2 and 3.1.3). • Three performance indicators such as: Output 3.1.3. is ”Enhanced application of, and compliance with, international labour standards through strengthened (i) labour inspection for improved compliance with labour legislation, and (ii) labour dispute resolution mechanisms and procedures”. • Performance indicator 3.1.1 (c) is similar to the UNSDCF indicator 4.6.3. Performance indicator 3.1.2(a) is “Number of governments (disaggregated by province) supported to develop and strengthen gender-responsive labour laws and rules in line with international labour standards and the recommendations”. ILO provided inputs into the UNSDCF 2023-2027 reflecting the need to implement recommendations of the issues raised by the ILO supervisory bodies.

description.narrative: The 2022 and 2023 reports to the CEACR were submitted in a timely manner and included replies to the comments of the supervisory bodies. Reports submitted in 2022 include C011, C087, C098 and C144. In 2023 reports were submitted on O01, C014 , C018, C019, C029, C045, C081, C089, C105, C 106, C118, C138 and C182. The ILO, with the support of the European Union, provided the following technical assistance: · ILO developed terms of reference (TOR) of the ILS Government Committee responsible for coordination of work on reports at federal and provincial levels and supported three meetings of the ILS Committee in May and June 2022, and May 2023 to capacitate its members, support development and implementation of the work plan and discuss and improve 2023 draft reports. · In 2023 ILO developed a technical note on the implementation of the latest recommendations of the CEACR concerning 14 ILO Conventions ratified by Pakistan. · ILO developed the capacity of tripartite constituents at the federal and provincial levels on the ILS supervisory system and reporting obligations through workshops organized in May and June 2022. · ILO conducted a detailed analysis of the gaps and problem areas on FOA/CB and developed a Technical Note on C.87 and C98 for four provinces and federal government and facilitated consultations in May 2023 for government, employers, and workers on this Technical Note. · ILO provided comments on the draft reports to the CEACR in 2022 and 2023.
